title: docs(scripts): the i18n gate class-8 abstentions name their counter, not a count
body:
Fixes #8102

Comment-only. No key, no locale pack, no assertion, no behaviour.

## Re-derived first, and the card was right about its subject but not complete

The dispatch required the numbers and key names to come from the gate's own run on
today's tree rather than from the card's prose. Run on `4b4d35a7d` (the branch point),
`node scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`:

```
Factory defaults tables: 32 createSafeTranslation site(s) over 32 distinct table(s) (0 unreadable) —
  846 row(s) compared against their en value, 846 matching, 0 on a key en does not define,
  0 with no single comparable en value, 0 unreadable.
```

and, reading the counters directly (`analyze(repoRoot)`), `factoryRows` 846,
`factoryComparedRows` 846, `factoryMatchingRows` 846, `factoryRowsNoEnKey` **0**,
`factoryUnjudgedRows` 0, `factoryUnreadableRows` 0, `factoryUnreadableTables` 0.

So the card is accurate about its own subject: the class-8 abstention list did say
*"The 5 such rows on this tree (`timeline.relative.*`, ...)"* and `factoryRowsNoEnKey`
is 0. Both sites it names exist verbatim.

**What the card did not have:** the same retired-five fact is carried five more times,
and the branch point had already moved past the number the card itself pasted (it quotes
841 compared at `924edd915`; the tree compares 846 today, because five unrelated rows
have been added since). Carriers of the falsified fact:

| where | text | verdict on `4b4d35a7d` |
|---|---|---|
| gate 412 | "The 5 such rows on this tree (`timeline.relative.*`, ...)" | false — 0 |
| gate 388 | "846 rows, 841 of them comparable against `en`" | 846 rows true, 841 comparable false — 846 |
| gate 450 | "the factory walk compares 841 rows" | false — 846 |
| gate 2016 | "a factory walk of 841 rows would otherwise mask a registry ..." | false — 846 |
| gate 2840 | "`factoryComparedRows` is 841" | false — 846 |
| pin 1410 | "`timeline.relative.*` is five such rows on `main` today." | false — 0 |
| pin 1673 | "the factory half's 841 rows would hide a registry ..." | false — 846 |

Two carriers of the *same* numbers were already in the durable form and are untouched:
gate 2827 *"`factoryComparedRows` **was** 841 over 32 tables **when the class landed**"*
and pin 1487 *"The measurement this class **shipped on**"*. Those declare their
measurement point, so they stay true. They are the model this PR copies.

## What is in scope, and the in-place extension

The claim declared the class-8 header prose plus the pin comment the card names. Rows
3-5 and 7 above are the same defect, the same fact, the same two files, mechanically
fixed into a form the same file already demonstrates, and no other open PR touches
either file (checked against all 12 open PRs). Correcting two carriers of one fact and
leaving five is the exact "one fact, N carriers, N-1 corrected" shape this card was
filed about, so all seven move together. **Declaring the surface increment here:** the
diff is the whole of both files' prose about these counters, not only the two lines
the card quotes.

## The form, and its named staleness mode

- **The abstention bullets name the counter they increment** — `factoryUnreadableTables`,
  `factoryUnreadableRows`, `factoryRowsNoEnKey`, `factoryUnjudgedRows` — instead of
  restating its value. All four print on the `Factory defaults tables:` line of every
  run. **Staleness mode: a renamed counter**, which is a rename inside the same file and
  fails loudly at the identifier, not silently in prose. The three bullets that said
  "0 on this tree" got the same treatment; leaving them restating a count while the
  fourth became derivable would have kept three-quarters of the rot mode in the list.
- **The worked example moves to the tense where it is permanently true.** The five rows
  were what only this counter could see, and once it did see them they were retired in
  objectui#7887. That is a *stronger* justification for printing the count than an
  occupied bucket ever was: the empty bucket is the outcome the printing bought, and
  the printing is what makes the next one visible. **Staleness mode: none** — it is a
  statement about objectui#7874/#7887, which do not move.
- **The shipping census keeps its numbers and declares its measurement point**
  ("the census objectui#7567 SHIPPED ON ... is a reading of the tree that card landed
  against"), then points at the summary line for today's. **Staleness mode: none** —
  a dated claim about a fixed commit range.
- **The three bare "841"s become "hundreds of rows"**, which is what those sentences
  actually argue (the factory number dwarfs the hand-rolled half's, so a combined
  counter would hide a collapse). **Staleness mode: it fails only if the factory walk
  drops below ~100 rows, which is far under the collapse floor of 500 that exits
  non-zero eight lines away.**

## What pins this header: nothing

Asked and answered both directions.

- **Nothing pins the prose.** No test reads `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` as
  text; no `check:*` script gates gate-header claims. That is why the sentence rotted
  in silence.
- **A pin in the same repo contradicted it.**
  `packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/timeline-relative-defaults-retired-7874.test.ts`
  asserts the five `timeline.relative.*` rows are absent, and
  `packages/test-support/src/defaults-table-scan.ts`'s header records the objectui#7887
  retirement. So the tree held a passing test and a header asserting the opposite fact.
- **The counter itself is unpinned, and that is a separate finding.** The hand-rolled
  half's case pins its abstentions — `handRolledRowsNoEnKey`, `handRolledUnjudgedRows`,
  `handRolledUnreadableRows`, `handRolledMatchingRows === handRolledComparedRows`. The
  factory half's case pins only `factoryUnreadableTables` and `factoryUnreadableRows`.
  `factoryRowsNoEnKey` going 5 -> 0 therefore failed nothing. Filed separately rather
  than ridden in here, because the dispatch's file surface is explicitly prose-only
  (see the report comment on #8102 for the conflict with the triage comment's route).

## Verification (real output)

All through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, parts joined with `&&` so the verdict covers
every one.

`node scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs && node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs && node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
-> `VERDICT command-exit 0`:

```
Factory defaults tables: 32 createSafeTranslation site(s) over 32 distinct table(s) (0 unreadable) —
  846 row(s) compared against their en value, 846 matching, 0 on a key en does not define,
  0 with no single comparable en value, 0 unreadable.
Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2976 keys), ...
OK  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6662 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).
Compared the working tree with 4b4d35a7d (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed,
  0 of them published source of a package the release covers, ... 0 changeset(s) added.
OK  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

**Changeset: checked, not guessed — none is owed**, so no `.changeset/*.md` and no
`skip-changeset` label (this repo declares "no release" with an empty-frontmatter
changeset when one is owed; here the gate says nothing is).

`pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts`
-> `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 137 passed (137)`,
run from the repo root against the root config.

`node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs && pnpm exec eslint THE_TWO_FILES`
-> `VERDICT command-exit 0`; the corpus sweep reports its standing objectui#7882
residue (1 file, unchanged by this PR) and eslint is silent.

`turbo ls --affected` against `4b4d35a7d`: **0 packages** — the diff is two root-level
`scripts/` files, so no package suite is owed. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the rest of the
`check:*` farm are declared to CI; this is a narrowed local run.

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test THE_TWO_FILES` ->
`NOT GOVERNED`. The PR stays **draft** regardless, per the dispatch.
